extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in social reform, women's rights, and early-20th-century feminist criticism (magazine readership)
extracted.subtask_description: Producing or evaluating persuasive magazine essays and reviews on women's roles, suffrage, child culture, education, and social reform—balancing evidence, ethical claims, and programmatic prescriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for legitimate opposition to woman suffrage
rubrics_metrics.description: There is but one reasonable way to oppose Woman Suffrage today: that is to bring definite proof that it has worked for evil in the states and countries where it has been long in practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition must show not merely that evil still exists but that new or greater evils exist and that these are proven due to use of the ballot by women. Avoid prophetic alarmism; rely on empirical, attributable evidence (e.g., accurate divorce statistics, proven causal links).

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance and centrality of the child as evaluative criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The child is the most important of personages; life should all be bent to its service; the woman's one, all-inclusive purpose is the right bearing and rearing of children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess works on child culture by how thoroughly they diagnose inadequacies in provision for child culture, mother preparation, home and school atmosphere, and by whether they offer concrete reforms (Ellen Key praised for stirring enthusiasm and revealing truth). Consider whether an author treats the child as central without ignoring broader social needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for motherhood-focused prescriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: An author who demands that women as a class consecrate themselves entirely to motherhood (foregoing education, profession, or other interests) should be evaluated on whether that exclusivity is justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between validating motherhood's importance and prescribing exclusive, soul-absorbing requirements; note where the author allows individual women choice versus demanding class-wide consecration. The reviewer agrees with child's centrality but criticizes absolute exclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational method standard: non-competitive, growth-centered schooling
rubrics_metrics.description: In education, with neither reward nor punishment as spur or bait; with no competition to rouse effort and animosity, but rather with the feeling of a gardener towards his plants; the teacher will teach and the children learn, in mutual ease and happiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate educational proposals by whether they promote individual development, avoid comparative ranking, and foster curiosity via presentation that arouses interest. Anti-patterns: reliance on competition, punishment, or measuring students against each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious/ethical evaluation by principle of loving service
rubrics_metrics.description: The feminine attitude in life brings into prominence the principle of loving service; religion seen from woman's viewpoint becomes a patient, practical fulfillment of law—a process of growth and comforting love and care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge religious or ethical writings by whether they emphasize growth, service, and practical care rather than reward/punishment narratives or combative doctrines. Note whether interpretations perpetuate androcentric readings or foreground loving service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for assessing social-political claims and facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors of fact in political argument are gross and unpardonable; claims such as divorce rates or lengths of suffrage must be checked against accessible facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and polemicists should verify statistics and historical claims (e.g., correct dates for suffrage adoption, accurate divorce trends) and avoid misattribution (e.g., correct authorship of The Woman's Bible). Anti-patterns include careless factual errors and misstatements used to bolster rhetoric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of alarmist/prophecy-based argumentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts that consist almost wholly of prophecies of horror about an untried process (e.g., woman suffrage) are weak; prophetic alarm must be replaced by factual study of real effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique speculative, fearful projections and require concrete empirical evidence of harms. Favor analyses grounded in reported experience from jurisdictions where the innovation exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure of women's political influence by legislative outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: In those countries and in our own states where women are already full citizens, the legislation introduced and promoted by them is of the same beneficent character; this record is a test of women's political effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the impact of women's suffrage by surveying enacted legislation and its character (beneficent vs. harmful). Use women's clubs and legislative records as empirical indicators rather than hypothetical fears.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for domestic labor reform (Nun in the Kitchen)
rubrics_metrics.description: We need, to keep the world well fed and really clean, skilled, specialized, experienced, well-paid workers; and it is none of our business whether they are married or single.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate proposals about household labor by whether they treat domestic work as skilled, deserving stable training and pay, rather than as transient, unpaid or untrained female servitude. Anti-patterns: reliance on a shifting, inexperienced pool of servants and maintaining servants' poverty/chastity/submission as social assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of social customs and 'society' roles
rubrics_metrics.description: With all women full human beings, trained and useful in some form of work; the class of busy idlers who run about forever 'entertaining' and being 'entertained' will disappear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge social commentary by whether it links social evils (idle 'society' roles, prostitution) to structural lack of meaningful work for women, and whether it proposes practical social integration via paid, honored employment for women.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for evaluating books on social reform (qualities valued in a book)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sincerity, boundless love and sympathy, widest and most searching observation; the power to throw a relentless light on cheap and trivial ways of facing grave issues and to stir enthusiasm for reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing social reform literature, weigh the author's sincerity, depth of observation, emotional appeal, and practical influence (e.g., stirring movements or changing attitudes). Consider whether key chapters (e.g., 'The Education of the Child') deserve separate dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for judging sex-relationship and parentage arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Right parentage is the purpose of the whole scheme of sex-relationship; motherhood is the dominant factor and must be so considered in the interests of better parentage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess writings on sexual ethics and family by whether they prioritize selection for parenthood, the responsibilities of parentage, and reforms in education and opportunity to realize better parentage. Distinguish advocacy for improved parentage from punitive or coercive measures.
